poem: your voice rings out with words that fill the room with sound, / but don't translate to actions when the rubber meets the ground. / you wrap your thoughts in phrases, smooth and full of spin, / just so you can hear yourself talk in a wordy, empty din.

you claim your steady pace is the mark of true grace, / but your stuff's always behind schedule, late or out of place. / you treat deadlines like optional, extra-time, / and call it "taking your time" - sounds more like a crime.

you're always on the clock, obsessed with every tick, / you judge the world from your superiority stick. / you smile when others miss the train, that smug old beam, / as if your rigid schedule is some perfect little dream.

your words do have a rhythm, smooth and full of flow, / but half the time it's showy fluff, not thoughts to know. / you say you love to speak and share what's on your mind, / but it all sounds the same - just you, again, redefined.

you speak of discipline like it's a noble, strict code, / when all we get is fortune-cookies wrapped in the same old light. / you claim to offer wisdom, deep insights to bite, / but you're just a clockwork dummy, no joy in your load.

you claim to keep it humble, but your stories scream brag, / a mask of confidence you wear because it was sold. / you say you're bold and sure, but it feels more like cold, / your "low-key" moments are just bragging by tag.

you talk about your loyalty, like it's carved in a bone, / book that won't stop listing facts in the most boring state. / you call yourself well-informed, acting like some old date- / but it's just a way to smother folks and keep them your own.

you claim you're caring, always there to tend, / but recklessness is what you sell to every goal. / you boast you're full of daring, a bold, bold soul, / but no one wants a mother who won't leave them friend.

you stroll through life at some eternal, sleepy pace, / but that's just how you let your chances escape your fate. / you say you're patient, always choosing to wait, / while deadlines overtake you in your cozy, lazy place.

you call yourself wise and so very bright, / then wheeze through a laugh like you're choking on smoke. / you claim to be hilarious, but your punchlines just choke, / but you're just a fortune cookie without any insight.
you live by rules, a perfect, ticking code, / a human clock that never dares to cheer. / your life is all routine and spinning gear, / but where's the joy? you're just a boring ode.

you say you're musical, like you've got magic strings, / when every conversation gets hit with your worst life choice. / you call yourself a sage with a deep, wise voice, / but bring a guitar to parties just to break a few things.

you love the game of everything, like every chat's a flame to chase, / but all you ever drop is old sayings wrapped in bad phrasing twice. / you say you've got such wisdom, a mind full of sage advice, / just so you can argue, score points, and act like you won first place.

you tell a joke so forced it's sure to choke, / but only 'cause you yell - not anyone else's fight. / you're always in the light, the life of every night, / then snort like it's the funniest thing you've spoke.

you boast of every trip as if it's some grand tale, / yet repeat the same stories, one monotonous robe. / you claim to know the world like the back of your globe, / but all we hear is "bali" until it turns completely pale.

you tout your thrift as wisdom, calling others unwise, / but all we see is stubbornness that makes you blind to your lies. / you call it smart to hoard like scrooge, you're just trying to save, / not daring to spend for joy - just too cheap to be brave.

you pride yourself on always staying perfectly on track, / but scream at anyone who dares to be a second late, full hack. / you set your watch by punctuality's strict, narrow clock, / then judge the rest of us with cold, unfeeling shock.

you've got that creative spark - great, now let's see it spark / something finished once, instead of art that stays in the park. / you're calm as a still pond - so still, it's like you're asleep, / zoning out when action spills and no one else would nap so deep.

you act like patience gives you saintly calm and endless grace, / but your work's always late, and you're last in the race. / you claim you're so patient, but you barely make a move, / your slowness keeps you stuck where nobody can groove.

you call yourself so chill, a breeze without a will, / but all you do is wreck the room and leave the feelings cold. / you tout your honesty as bold, your truth always well-told, / just coasting through life, avoiding work, avoiding skill.

you love your words like poetry and praise your perfect flow, / it's just a monologue - no one else gets to show. / you claim your voice brings clarity and power to the speech, / but all we hear is ego making trust a total breach.

you boast your world is vast and rich and wide, / but your stories have no place but bali as your home. / you say your soul was meant to roam and roam, / but all you talk about is bali with such pride.

you praise your polished speech, a waterfall of grace, / just trying to drown us out with your self-made chase. / you love the sound of words, not meaning or the ground, / it's showy, empty noise with no truth to be found.
you say you're in it for the long hard core, / but your idea of fun's closing every door. / you set such a fast and furious pace, / there's no time left to show your human face.
you brag about your calm, slow-moving flow, / but time has left you stuck way far below. / you call your slowness a steady, noble pace, / while life zooms by and you lose every race.

you act like calmness is some special kind of breeze, / but even your keys need shaking just to find the keys. / you float through life without a care to drift, / unless someone else will do the work to lift.

you're a master of the plan, the ultimate planner, so neat, / but your obsession with control drives everyone up the street. / you dish out wisdom like a sage dropping every quote, / yet no one asked for your life lessons scribbled on every note.

you talk about the stars and how you'd carry me to the moon, / then gift a syrupy playlist that makes my ears want to spoon. / you set up candlelit dinners like a movie's final scene, / but it's so overdone it feels like your tired love routine.

you pride yourself on being perfect on the clock, / but throw a tantrum if someone dares be even slightly off the block. / you hold the door like you're the keeper of the gate, / and sigh so loud if anyone else has to wait.

you love your flow of polished, practiced prose, / a monologue you're always trying to compose. / your words are loud, your meaning sounds profound, / but when you're done, no one's still standing 'round.

you talk about your humility, that soft, unassuming glow, / but it's just a mask to drop a trophy into everyone's show. / you claim to be so down-to-earth, no shine, no glint of gold, / yet you've got a whole scrapbook of stories you've already told.

you call yourself a genius, always using that big brain, / but all you do is correct others and never refrain. / you preach your perfect diet like some holy, clean creed, / while judging every meal i eat like it's a crime to feed.
you boast of worldly lore and every tale, / but all you do is bore us with your bali trail. / you're not a traveler - you're just stuck on a map, / reliving "back when" in a nostalgia trap.

you brag about your perfect sense of clock, / but it's just a throne you guard - like time is only yours to mine. / you think your schedule's flawless, sacred and divine, / but throw a fit if someone's just one minute off the block.

you think you're hilarious? your punchlines just smoke. / you crack yourself up while the rest of us choke. / you love being spontaneous, ditching any plan, / but chaos is the only thing you really can.

you think you're swiss - you never miss the clock, / but throw a delay in, and it gives you such a shock. / you pride yourself on always being on the track, / but what you really have is a complete lack...

you boast about having a big, warm, and giving heart, / but i just want to charter a ship to escape your advice and chart. / you say you're kind and always so thoughtfully kind, / but sometimes i just want to lock you out of my mind.

you boast about your steady, thoughtful pace, / but nothing's ever finished in its rightful place. / you say you're patient when you make us wait, / like time is on your side - and it just isn't your fate.
you call your penny-pinching habits being smart, / but there's no generosity left in your heart. / you count each dime with obsessive pride, / and waste the time we have by splitting every ride.

you loudly claim your patience is a gift without compare, / but it's just an excuse to stall and delay everything you care. / you treat each task like it's a precious hour, / when you're still half-finished, it's progress - just not power.

you tell me your new painting's done, and ask if i can view it online, / but it's not finished, not completed, and there's no real surprise or shine. / you say you're serious, but it's not a joke, still, it lacks a twist or flair, / it's artistic, yes - but not so funny - though you claim it is everywhere.

you're always on track, always ahead of the clock, / but judge the rest by how fast you think they should walk. / you pride yourself on showing up at the perfect rate, / then slam the door like you run the place and not just the gate.

you claim your calm is tried and true, it's passed each test, / but we're all bored stiff waiting for your eternal rest. / you talk about your steady, zen-like pace, / then wonder why your work's still in the same place.
you spin your stories like a one-man globe, / but it's just a tour guide in a casual robe. / you bring up "bali" with every single tale, / as if no one else has ever looked at a sunset or gone pale.
you call your penny-pinching habits being smart, / but there's no generosity left in your heart. / you count each dime with obsessive pride, / and waste the time we have by splitting every ride.

you love that you're eloquent, always hitting the right tone, / it's less about ideas and more about your speaking throne. / you say you're so articulate, your words just never stop the flow, / it's less about the message and more about your verbal show.

you always see the silver lining in the sun, / but miss the storm right here where the real fun's undone. / you're always pushing hard to win the big race, / but only care if you're first - no one else gets a place.

you flex that silver tongue like a poet's sweet song, / but it's just a show-off monologue spinning too long. / you wrap your thoughts in metaphors, always trying to spin, / the truth is you're just talking to be heard - say it within.

you wear your calm like armor, full of patient grace, / but time is burning leaving you still stuck in second place. / you act like speed's a sin, you're wise and slow, / when everyone has moved on, you're still trying to go.

it takes forever to split a coffee - you're wasting everyone's time. / you boast about being frugal, as if it's something to be proud, / you track every penny like it's your last dime, / you count change in your head - we can all hear it out loud.

they call you 'diligent' and praise your effort and aim, / as if that's all there is to being stuck in a game. / you always put in hours, never seem to lag, / but rarely take time out to think beyond your bag.

you spin like a pro, spinning tales from each globe, / like you're paid to wear your passport on your robe. / you think your "bali days" make for a never-ending tale, / i'm half-convinced you'd send your life story in a postcard to your own mail.

your optimism's so bright, it blinds everyone in sight, / but it's just wishful thinking through even the darkest night. / you stick to every task like some kind of disciplined class, / a clockwork stiff with no spark and no room for a laugh or a pass.
you brag about your calm, slow-moving flow, / but time has left you stuck way far below. / you call your slowness a steady, noble pace, / while life zooms by and you lose every race.
you give your time, and you look like you care, / it's obvious you truly think you're rare. / your charm is fake, yet somehow still on show, / we're told we love it - and we all just go.
